How tide tables are built

Tide tables combine decades of harbour measurements with the pull of the moon and the sun. Forecasters fit a few dozen harmonic constituents to the recorded water levels, and the result predicts high and low water for each day of the coming year with an error of a few minutes.

Readers who want the raw method can read the harmonic analysis primer, which explains why the largest constituent follows the moon and why local geography changes everything else about a harbour.
